Note: For applicant see section 6."}],"answer":"The Manual describes a deferment of acceptance rather than requiring a separate extension request for an examination hearing.

• Hearing — Manual practice: If you request an ex parte hearing on an examination matter, the Registrar will defer acceptance automatically; you need not separately apply for an extension of time or deferment. The deferment ends when you withdraw the hearing request or when the Registrar decides to accept or reject the application, whichever happens first. [TMM/Part16/1/1/1; TMM/Part17/5/5/2]

• Time remaining after the hearing deferment — Manual practice: The annex records that the balance of time remaining before deferment remains available afterwards. In that sense, the acceptance clock is paused, rather than restarted with a fresh full period. [TMM/Part17/x-annex-a1---deferment-of-acceptance-date---grounds-and-time-limits#1]

• Court appeal or ART review — Manual practice: Once a court appeal has begun or an ART review application has been made, acceptance is deferred until three months after determination or other disposal, or until expiry of any further time allowed by the relevant court or ART. The Registrar enters the deferment on notification, provided the trade mark application is still pending. These passages concern appeals or reviews of the Registrar’s decision. [TMM/Part17/5/5/2]

• Act: Section 33(4) separately requires the Registrar to give the applicant an opportunity to be heard before rejecting the application. It does not itself specify the deferment timetable. [TMA1995/s33]

The timing explanation above is Manual practice, not a quotation of the Regulations: the relevant Regulations are not included in the supplied legislation. I cannot calculate your actual revised deadline from these passages alone."}
